$comment: Where a recipe variable's value comes from, and what the platform does with it. The schema's variableSource pattern only bounds the NAMESPACE of user and ticket-image values; this file closes the parts that are closed. Hand-edited, mirrored by variable-catalog.ts and VariableCatalog.cs, and held by verify-contract-parity.mjs plus a coverage test in each consumer.

user_fields.$comment: Every value the platform stores about the account holder. 'support' says whether a recipe may bind it; 'availability' whether a completed profile is guaranteed to have a value.

ticket_fields.$comment: The leaf of ticket.extracted.<leaf> is both the JSON key the vision model is asked to return and the selector of the normalizer applied to the answer. Membership is open — a portal may need a field no other portal has — but these leaf names carry a normalizer, and any other leaf is passed through as plain text.

ticket_request_fields.$comment: Values the account holder supplies WITH the ticket, as opposed to values read off its image. A closed set: each is a column the API writes at upload, so a source outside it cannot resolve. 'pattern' is the shape the value must have before it may reach a portal — it is typed into a third party's form, so it is validated where it enters and again where it is used. 'default_value' is what the executor resolves when the ticket carries none, which makes every field here available to a required variable.
